evidence: src/application/ports.ts: ProductRepository declares save(product: Product): void as the way to persist products.
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts addProduct: calls this.products.save(product), so new products are persisted through the port.

src/application/fulfilment-service.ts placeOrder: calls reserveStock(product, quantity) and, on rollback, releaseStock(r.product, r.quantity), but never calls this.products.save on the changed products. Only this.orders.save(order) is called.

src/application/fulfilment-service.ts cancelOrder: calls releaseStock(product, line.quantity) on products from this.products.get, but only calls this.orders.save(order), never this.products.save(product).
src/application/fulfilment-service.ts transition/cancelOrder: changed orders are always saved through this.orders.save, unlike changed products.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The two files cover one concern: fulfilment use cases (fulfilment-service.ts) and the repository ports they depend on (ports.ts). Errors and state transitions are handled consistently through domain functions (advance, cancel, reserveStock, releaseStock) and DomainError. The problem is how the service uses its own ProductRepository port. The port declares save(product), and addProduct persists through it. Order changes are also always saved: placeOrder, transition and cancelOrder each call this.orders.save(order). But the stock changes in placeOrder (reserveStock, plus releaseStock on rollback) and in cancelOrder (releaseStock) are never saved through this.products.save. They only persist because an in-memory repository hands back the same object reference. So the service goes around its own port contract for products, while it uses that contract correctly for orders. Any repository that stores copies, such as one backed by a database, would lose the stock changes. Because the abstraction is used inconsistently, the rubric is not met. I am only moderately confident: I could not see the domain files, so I could not check whether the stock validation in addProduct also exists there.

violations.message: Products are not persisted through the ProductRepository port declared in ports.ts. placeOrder and cancelOrder change product stock with reserveStock/releaseStock but never call this.products.save. They rely on the repository returning a shared mutable reference. Orders, by contrast, are always saved after changes, so the port is used inconsistently.
